name: Cascade
description: Replays little loops of what you just played, stacked at octave (and fifth) speeds in a pattern you can hear, so one note comes back as a shimmering, rhythmic cascade of itself.

params.name: Pattern
params.description: How a slice is replayed. Stack loops it at several speeds at once, Restrike strikes its start again and again, Drone holds a short piece, Steps climbs like an arpeggio.

params.name: Time
params.description: How long after a note it first comes back, and the pulse its repeats fall on. Short times give a fast glittering stutter; long times replay whole phrases.

params.name: Repeats
params.description: How many times each slice comes back before it stops, which sets how long the cascade goes on after you stop playing.

params.name: Decay
params.description: How much quieter and darker each repeat is than the one before. Fully down, every repeat is as loud and as bright as the first.

params.name: High
params.description: Level of the replays that run faster than you played. They sound an octave or more above and come round two or four times in the space of one slower repeat.

params.name: Low
params.description: Level of a half-speed replay: the slice an octave down and twice as long, underneath the rest and in the middle of the stereo picture.

params.name: Interval
params.description: Which speeds the faster replays use. Octaves stays on the note you played. Octaves and fifths adds replays a fifth above, which fall three against two with the rest.

params.name: Shape
params.description: The envelope of every replay. Low gives sharp plucked fronts that die away; high makes each one swell in and out, so the pattern blurs into a wash.

params.name: Reverse
params.description: The chance that a replay runs backwards. Fully down everything runs forwards; fully up everything runs backwards.

params.name: Spread
params.description: How far the replays are placed to the left and right. The faster ones sit furthest out and swap sides as they repeat.

params.name: Tone
params.description: Takes the highs off all the replays. Lower settings make the cascade softer and further away.

params.name: Mix
params.description: Balance between the dry signal and the cascade.

origin.note: Written for live-mix on cpp/kit. In outline: the input is cut into slices on a clock that restarts at note onsets, and each slice is replayed by a pool of windowed loop voices at speeds of 1/2, 1, 3/2, 2, 3 and 4, in one of four patterns. Replaying windowed fragments of sound at other speeds is after the approach of Curtis Roads, 'Microsound'. The faster voices read half-band decimated copies of the buffer so that they do not alias: pre-filtered copies at halved resolutions, after the approach of Lance Williams, 'Pyramidal Parametrics', applied to audio. The Drone pattern cuts its loop to a whole number of cycles found with a normalised difference function, after the approach of A. de Cheveigne and H. Kawahara, 'YIN, a fundamental frequency estimator for speech and music'; where the sound has no cycle to cut on, the two voices that hand the loop to each other cross over at equal power instead. The sources are cited from memory and no constants or details were taken from them. Not a model of any particular unit.
